output.brief: The rise in store 14's shrink may not be real. The Q1–Q3 figures are estimates from partial cycle counts, with an error of about ±0.6 points per quarter. Chain history shows that about half of stores with two straight estimated rises were not confirmed by the year-end full count. Store 14's full-count shrink has run 1.5–1.8% in past years. The recorded shoplifting incidents rose chain-wide after the incident app launched on 1 April, so Pask's rising log counts say little about actual theft. The ethics tip about the night stocker was checked on CCTV and found to be routine cardboard runs. The sales mix did not change. The neighbouring stores did not rise, but that does not clear or convict the self-checkout lanes. I can't tell which cause, if any, is real. Next steps: keep store 14 in the 7 December full count and decline Regional Operations' request to skip it. Hold off on a guard, pulling the self-checkout lanes, and any action against the stocker until the count result is compared with the interim figures. Doubling cycle counts adds little precision. If the full count confirms a rise, look at the lanes, customer theft and staff theft, starting with shrink by item type. I'm fairly confident in this call.
